summary: Di Jiang works in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. They have held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.

Di Luo specializes in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. They earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (attested 2016), supervised by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge, after completing an MA under James Steele.

Diana L. Eck is an indologist and scholar of religion. She earned her BA at Smith College, MA at SOAS, and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, where she served as a professor from circa 1976 to 2022.

Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at Leipzig, Tibet University, Humboldt University, EPHE, and Sorbonne, and held posts including research assistant and professor at Humboldt University, and Principal Investigator at Hamburg (2021–2025).

Diane A. Lichtenstein completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an adjunct professor of anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane Denis specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned a BA from Naropa University and a PhD from Laval University (2005–2013), and served as an associate professor at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 2017.

Diane E. Riggs is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UCLA under William M. Bodiford and held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She was attested in 1982 as a graduate student at McMaster University, where she studied under Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the Catholic University of America (attested 1974) under the supervision of Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli earned his PhD at École Polytechnique, where he was supervised by Francisco Varela.

Diego Loukota (1985–2024) worked in Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Bologna, Peking University under Qing Duan, and UCLA (PhD, 2014–2019), later serving as an assistant professor at UCLA (circa 2022–2024).

Dieter B. Kapp (1941–2021) was an indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate under Hermann Berger and his habilitation at Heidelberg, later directing the Institut für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (1990–2006).
Dieter Conrad (1932–2001) worked in Indology and related fields. He earned his Dr.iur. at Heidelberg University (circa 1957–1963), where he served as a Senior Research Fellow from 1963 to 1997.

Dieter George (1935–1985) was an indologist and historian. He earned his PhD at Marburg under Wilhelm Rau, worked at the Royal Library of Berlin (circa 1972–1985), and served as Geschäftsführer of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1977–1985).

Dieter Gunkel is a linguist and indologist. He earned a BA at Middlebury and a PhD at UCLA, and held posts at the University of Munich, University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA (Associate Professor, 2024).

Dieter Schlingloff is an indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Ernst Waldschmidt, completed degrees at Göttingen and Humboldt, and held professorial posts at Kiel (1968–1971), Munich (1972–1996), and Leipzig (2005).
Dieter Schrapel is an indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1970) under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978–2007) and founded and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Diether Lauenstein (1914–1990) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen, earned a Dr.theol. at Marburg under Johannes Nobel, habilitated at Greifswald, and held a post at Greifswald in 1944.

Dietmar Rothermund (1933–2020) was a historian and indologist. He studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, circa 1956–1959), and held the Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University (1968–2001).
